articleTitle: Control Strategy for Virtual Synchronous Generator Based on Y-Z Source Inverter in Islanded Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) concept stands as a strategy for the seamless integration of renewable energy sources into the grid. In scenarios where symmetrical and sinusoidal operating conditions are lacking, VSMs demonstrate multifaceted capabilities. They can operate as power sources especially in islanded-systems, adeptly address harmonic distortions and imbalances, offer load power compensation, and elevate voltage quality at the grid. Even so, dead time variations, discontinuous input current, and non-single-power-stage configuration of conventional voltage/current source inverters and also, load variation can result in VSMs behaving as harmonic and imbalance absorbers. This paper utilizes a specific Y-Source Inverter (YZSI) for the first time as a solution to these challenges. Through integrating this innovative configuration with an exceptionally adaptable voltage gain and an enhanced multi-loop control strategy into an isolated power system accommodating diverse load profiles, it not only achieves high efficiency in power transfer but also enhances overall system performance quality. Furthermore, it contributes to extending the lifespan and preserving the quality of the input source. The controller is designed to regulate system frequency, voltage, and manage voltage and current for YZSI, delivering impressive performance even in non-ideal grid conditions. MATLAB/Simulink confirms the efficacy of the proposed YZSI VSG control strategy with a high accuracy achieved through a comprehensive examination of the internal component parameters.

articleTitle: Impact of Charging Speed on Electric Vehicle Battery Life
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The growing concerns about climate change have led to the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce global carbon emissions. Li-ion batteries have become prominent in EVs because of their high density and fast charging capability. However, there are several limitations associated with the technologies. Therefore, this paper aims to investigate the impact of charging rate on Li-ion batteries used in EVs. Four chargers, i.e. 6A, 12A, 24A and 48A chargers, are used to charge EV batteries rated 48V and 24Ah. Two models consisting of theoretical and practical designs are developed in MATLAB/Simulink platform to verify the results. Different Li-ion battery parameters are evaluated for battery degradation, including state of charge (SOC), battery cell temperature, charging current, cycling period, discharging current, and depth of discharge (DOD). The result showed an increased charging rate drains the battery faster than slow chargers. Other factors influencing battery degradation include temperature, SOC, DOD and cycling period. Proper management and avoiding deep discharge of the battery is recommended to prolong its lifespan.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fuzzy Logic Controller-Based Energy Management Systems for FCEVs via Genetic Algorithm and Big Bang-Big Crunch
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study proposes an optimized Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) as an Energy Management System (EMS) for Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEVs). The primary objective is to efficiently meet the power demand required for vehicle propulsion while judiciously utilizing available energy sources. Initially, a generic two-input single-output FLC is designed. Subsequently, optimization is conducted to determine the optimal combination of input/output membership functions to operate both energy sources sufficiently. The optimization is intended to minimize a target objective function using two global optimization algorithms, Big Bang-Big Crunch (BBBC) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Simulations and analysis are conducted to validate the performance of the optimized FLCs compared to the generic FLC. Results indicate that the optimized FLCs operate the system efficiently while meeting the power requirements and validating the system constraints.

articleTitle: Development of High-Voltage Short-Pulse Signal Generator for Ultrasonic Transducer Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: High-voltage short-pulse generators play a crucial role in diverse applications within both industrial and biomedical sectors. Among these applications, one notable example is its use in industrial 5-l0 MHz ultrasonic transducers, which require sub-100ns high negative voltage pulse for measuring pipeline thickness and offering up to 0.1 mm precision. However, generating these signals is a challenging task. In this paper, two circuit techniques have been proposed to generate high-voltage short-pulse signals. The first circuit utilizes a combination of a variable resistor and a variable capacitor to adjust the width of the generated signal. It also incorporates two inverters and a power MOSFET to generate a high negative voltage pulse. This circuit successfully generates a -150V pulse with a duration of 75ns. The second circuit relies solely on a variable capacitor to control the pulse width. It includes a logic circuit and a power BJT to produce a high negative pulse, resulting in a -220V pulse with a width of 90µs. Both circuits have been verified either by simulation or experimental testing.

articleTitle: Enhanced Millimeter-Wave Communication and Radar Systems in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of IEEE 802.11ad wireless communication protocol into millimeter-wave radar systems, especially the impact of the vehicle scheduling policy after collision on the performance of the system. By embedding radar functionality within the standard communication protocol, various scheduling algorithms, such as Greedy, Proportional Fairness (PF), Round-Robin (RR), and Randomized Algorithm (RA), are evaluated for their impact on system throughput and radar overhead. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of these algorithms in optimizing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and throughput during vehicle movement. Finally, we propose to explore adaptive strategies based on real-time network conditions to dynamically balance throughput and fairness in the future to improve the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptation Strainer Block Detection for Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning System of Urban Metro Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Along with the rapid development of urban metro transportation, the operating mode of heating ventilation and air conditioning system becomes diversified and self-adaptive, which results in significant differences in health status of strainers assembled in separated units. So far, the maintenance of strainers has been proceeded periodically regardless of confirming the actual status of individual parts, as a result, the maintenance strategy intends to purify or replace [1] the ones which are not too dirty to degrade the air conditioning performance [2]. On the other hand, the strainers are more likely to be dirty in summer than other seasons [3], and the suggestion of periodic maintenance remains the same after rolling stock delivered, hence the over maintenance of strainers is a common issue for urban metro transportation. Many researches and efforts have devoted to this field, the most popular solution is to install pressure transducers [4] to monitor the difference between two sides of the strainer. It does help to improve the efficiency of maintenance, however strict limitations, such as refurbishment of existed rolling stocks, unstable detection of sensors, unpredictable changes of real-time thresholds, remains not solved which makes the solution difficult to widely applied. In the aim to reduce the over maintenance and waste of spare parts without installing new sensors or devices, the essay introduces a comprehensive model to estimate the health level of strainers. The model is trained based on ten-dimensional real-time train-borne data, including three-phase currents of motors, mode of dampers, etc., and K-means is adapted to improve the accuracy of strainers block detection. The model converges to four levels of blocking risks: none, low, medium and high, the simulation results generated by model matches the experiment data. Finally, the essay discusses the benefits of wide application and suggests rolling-stock maintenance from periodic mode to status-driven mode.

articleTitle: Enhancing Malware Detection with Firefly and Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Malware poses a serious threat to computer networks, user privacy, and user systems. Effective cybersecurity depends on the correct detection and classification of malware. In order to improve the effectiveness of malware detection systems, this research paper explores the application of two optimization algorithms, Firefly Algorithm (FA) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), for feature selection in the context of malware detection using the CIC-MaIMem-2022 dataset. Leveraging Python for implementation and employing Random Forest (RF) as the clas-sification model, the study compares the performance of FA and GWO in enhancing malware detection accuracy. Results indicate that the RF model with FA achieves remarkable metrics, boasting an accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score of 99.97%, along with a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 99.95%. In contrast, the GWO-based approach yields an accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score of 99.95%, accompanied by an MCC of 96.88%. The findings highlight the efficacy of FA over GWO in optimizing feature selection for enhancing malware detection accuracy, providing valuable insights for future research in cybersecurity..

articleTitle: A Path Tracking and Collision Prevention Control System for an Electric Vehicle with Trajectories Generated by Bezier Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The problem of trajectory generation and tracking for stable road line tracking and collision avoidance systems for electric vehicles has become a trending topic for which different solutions have been discussed by researchers working in the field of control theory and industry stakeholders. In the trajectory generation phase for path following and object avoidance problems, researchers have tried to find solutions by linear interpolation on points generated by Bezier curves, which are two-dimensional B-spline curves. This study proposes and discusses a method for autonomous driving by means of PID, LQR and hybrid PID+LQR control methods whose parameters are found by using genetic algorithm and whose trajectories are automatically generated by Bezier curves for road following and object avoidance situations.

articleTitle: Exploiting Flexible Memristor Based on Carbon Quantum Dots for Neuromorphic Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Flexible memristors based on carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are explored in this study, representing a pivotal advancement in non-volatile memory technology within the realm of portable artificial intelligence. Leveraging the exceptional flexibility and stability of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates, these devices demonstrate resistance switching characteristics akin to their initial state despite enduring multiple instances of destructive folding. Notably, analyses including current-voltage curve (I-V) assessments and long-term potentiation/long-term depression (LTP/LTD) evaluations reinforce this resilience. Furthermore, these devices exhibit classical synaptic behaviors, such as spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), paired-pulse facilitation (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PPF$</tex>), and the transition from short-term memory (STM) to long-term memory (LTM). This research represents a significant stride towards the advancement of the next generation of flexible memory devices.

articleTitle: Robust Controller Design for Longitudinal and Lateral Model of High-Performance Fixed-Wing UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study focuses on designing and analyzing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{2}$</tex> control algorithms for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with reference tracking control objective under disturbances. Two different robust control strategies, developed based on the linearized UAV mathematical model, are implemented in the inner loop defined as the angular velocity control loop in the nonlinear mathematical model to enhance the performance of attitude angular velocity by improving the robustness against disturbances. This papaer also includes disturbance effects on UAVs such as gust model and time-dependent change of the centre of gravity model. The results of the two different control algorithms are compared and presented in terms of time-domain specifications.

articleTitle: Joint Angle Estimation in Beam-Space Based on the Information of Range-Sum for Bistatic MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Bistatic MIMO radar can simultaneously estimate the direction of departure (DOD) and direction of arrival (DOA) of the target. However, traditional bistatic MIMO radar DOD and DOA estimation methods need a two-dimensional (2D) search, which requires a lot of computation. This paper focuses on the Capon angle estimation algorithm in beam-space for bistatic MIMO radar. The relationship between the DOD and the DOA is obtained by using the information of range-sum. Using this angle relation in beam conversion matrix design and angle search not only reduces the signal dimension, but also transforms the 2D search algorithm into the one-dimensional (1D) search for DOD or DOA. Therefore, the computation is reduced effectively and the angle measurement accuracy is improved. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is superior to the traditional methods in angle measurement accuracy under the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: A New Routing Algorithm Based on an Efficient Cluster-Head Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) was been applied in various fields to ease our daily life. Thus, the researchers concentrate more attention on the different problems related to wireless networks. The most serious problem is the limited energy of sensors due to their tiny battery. Therefore, minimizing the consumed network energy is the major concern of the WSN. Several works have been designed to save the network energy. However, this problem still paralyzed network communication. The clustering technique is an effective solution based on organizing the sensors into clusters, where a node is selected to play the role of the Cluster Head(CH) to aggregate the collected data and send them to the sink node. The selection of the CHs is an important task owing to the various tasks attributed to these nodes. This work aims to manage the problem of energy using two stages: the first aims to activate only sensors sensing enough signal, and the second selects effectively the network CHs. A hybrid strategy was been utilized in the second stage, where the multi-criteria decision-making method and an optimal cost function were been combined. Simulation results have proved the efficiency of the proposed method compared to the HEED protocol.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Drone Path Planning in Forest Firefighting
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In recent years, forest fire disasters are receiving much more attention due to climate change, globally. Previous methods using machine learning algorithms to fight fires have progressed substantially over the past years. However, they have faced challenges such as the lack of evaluation and implementation of fire extinguishing systems, difficulties in handling multiple spot fires, and inadequate management of time and resources. Multi-objective optimization (MOP) is a mathematical method for solving optimization problems involving multiple conflicting objectives. Compared with traditional heuristic algorithms such as genetic algorithms, Particle swarm optimization (PSO) usually has a faster convergence speed and is easy to parallel. Therefore, this paper combines the PSO algorithm with the MOP algorithm and uses the Multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm to solve this problem. Firstly, multiple data factors in the fire field are weighted and assigned, and multiple fire scenes are scored according to the weighted values. Then, based on these scores, the PSO is run. At the same time, a real and dynamic 3D simulation environment was built by preprocessing and in-depth analysis of the existing mountain fire data. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better search effect and path planning method under the premise of ensuring effective stability. Its algorithm stability is increased by 19.96% and the average value of fitness function decreased by 35.5%.

articleTitle: Design of a 3-dB Directional Coupler in S-Band Using Symmetric Coupled-Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, analysis and design of a 3-dB <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> directional coupler operating in S-band is proposed. The coupler employs symmetrical multi-section coupled lines designed in a strip line technique. The theory of symmetrical directional coupler synthesis method was employed to achieve results for the ideal conditions. Subsequently, through a tuning process, the objective was to adjust these results using full-wave EM simulation to obtain a balanced coupler design concerning amplitude and phase response. The simulation results show that the coupler maintains magnitude consistency within ± 0.3 dB, isolation and return loss parameters are better than 16 dB and phase difference between two output ports is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$88^{\mathrm{o}}\pm 0.6^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> in 1.7 - 4.35 GHz frequency range. This simulation results indicate an improvement which is achieved in fractional bandwidth (FBW) performance around the center frequency (fo = 3 GHz).

articleTitle: A 25–34 GHz Power Amplifier Based on Differential Layout in 40 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a front-end module (FEM) with linear power amplifier (PA) using a 40-nm bulk CMOS technology. For circuit structure, the amplifier is designed as an easy single casco de stage with neutralization capacitors and transformers. In addition, a novel differential layout is proposed and applied in design to eliminate considerable parasitic parameters and improve the amplification capability. At the center frequency of near 30 GHz, the P A achieves gain (S21) of 14.5~ 17.5 dB, output power at 1-dB compression point <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{OP}_{1\text{dB}})$</tex> of 17.49 dBm and power added efficiency (P AE) of 26%.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Integrating Distributed Generations in Unbalanced Distribution Network by Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In recent years, Distributed Generation (DG) have been a high penetration rate in the distribution network. Planning the active power of electricity from DG can save energy from grid side and reduce power losses in the unbalanced distribution system by considering the capacity to generate electricity. This research was aimed to appropriately generate the active power of DG for managing the energy on grid side and enable distributed system operators (DSO) can forecast production capabilities, maintain the grid balancing, and ensuring the stability of the distribution system. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm was implemented in MATLAB for optimal active power for each DG using Peer-to-Peer (P2P) communication with DIgSILENT for power flow analysis by shared data via comma-separated values file. Additionally, specifying equality and inequality constraint were applied. The results indicated that the active power of DG who is injected to the grid effect to the total power loss, voltage deviation, and power flow direction. In conclusion, the DSO can use them as the considerate guideline for issuing commands to adjust the increase or decrease in the production capacity of DG within reliability and security of the distributed system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power Distribution Network Reliability: A Comparative Analysis of Strategic Modifications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Modern electrical distribution networks shaped by technological advancements and urban expansion, ensuring enhanced service quality parameters has become imperative for efficient operation. Consequently, evaluating the reliability associated with power system outages has become a standard practice during the decision-making process of power system network design. This evaluation is crucial to ensure a consistent and reliable power supply for customers. This paper focuses on a comprehensive reliability study conducted on a typical power distribution feeder structure. The objective is to identify the existing reliability indices of the system within the evolving technological and urban landscape. Subsequently, various network modification options and innovative protection philosophy approaches are introduced to bolster the system's reliability. Following a thorough evaluation of diverse modification proposals, this study concludes that the optimal enhancement, in terms of reliability, involves altering the operational scenario for the first supply feeder from the source. Specifically, maintaining all the normally open breakers as closed in the feeders structured above, each rated at 33 KV. This strategic modification ensures a resilient power distribution network, aligning seamlessly with the demands of contemporary urban environments and technological advancements.

articleTitle: Back-to-Back MMC Converter for Railway Application Using Averaged Submodules Model
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Thanks to their flexibility, modular multilevel converter, also known as MMC, are in the spotlights to help modernize railway infrastructures. To comply with power quality issues in presence of high harmonics components and high-power changes, it's mandatory to provide resilient converters. This article introduces an architecture solution based on MMC converters to provide a 25 kV-50 Hz power supply complying with industry standards. Dynamic performances are analyzed using different kind of load and the back-to-back configuration is validated using averaged sub-modules to ease computation issues.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy of Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle with Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this study, using a car model equipped with a fuel cell stack and battery, the Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) method is used to control energy in the system. The Toyota Mirai car's specifications are used to make this model. Formulas for classical vehicle dynamics are explained first, followed by a discussion of electrical circuit formulas. The methods used for the fuel cell are established, the parameters are chosen and studied for the used DRL. For rewarding, a cost function has been developed. It is decided which parameters need to be included in this cost function. The DRL agent with the incentives is trained and then validated in a simulation environment based on the precedence of these parameters. A chosen driving cycle has been used to validate this technique. Consequently, the intended energy management system is deployed in the simulation environment and an agent capable of tracking the driving cycle is acquired. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the employed method.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for NMR Comagnetometer Gyroscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Machine learning is a very popular method used today to solve many complex and nonlinear problems for optimization purposes. This paper investigates the application of Artificial Neural Network (ANN), which is one of the machine learning methods, in a Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Comagnetometer Gyroscope (CG) experiment. It has been determined that T2 (transverse relaxation time) and SNR (signal-to-noise ratio), which are the two most critical parameters for NMR CG performance, can be estimated using environmental and physical quantities. In this way, the T2 of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">129</sup>Xe and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sup>Xe was estimated at 0.0722 and 0.0720 RMSE (root mean square error), respectively. The SNR of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">129</sup>Xe and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sup>Xe was also estimated at 0.0794 and 0.0816 RMSE using the same method. The results showed that the T2 and SNR parameters for both <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">129</sup>Xe and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sup>Xe isotopes can be predicted without measuring them by developing an appropriate prediction model. This implementation can also make significant contributions to the optimization of NMR CG performance.

articleTitle: Power Optimization of LCRC for A Custom PCI Express 6.0 IP Core
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) protocol has gained extensive adoption in all computing systems. Due to the rising computational demands in edge devices, PCIe interfaces are now becoming prevalent in mobile computing systems as well. While PCIe devices employ Link-Level Cyclic Redundancy Control (LCRC) to ensure high-performance operations without compromising data integrity, this crucial feature significantly contributes to the overall power consumption. In this work, we introduce a new LCRC calculation method specifically tailored to mitigate energy usage and reduce power consumption in LCRC, offering insights into the interplay between data integrity, power consumption, and overall system performance for a custom PCIe 6.0 IP core. Our design achieves higher speeds as the CDC modules required in CRC calculation were eliminated, thus enabling relaxed timing and increased performance. Throughput per consumed energy has also been increased, improving the overall energy efficiency. Our design approach enables minimizing power consumption while maintaining the robust error-checking capabilities of the LCRC mechanism. The proposed solution establishes a balance between performance, power efficiency, and reliability in PCle-enabled devices. We have evaluated the performance of the proposed approach in terms of energy efficiency, area, and speed. In addition, we also discussed the performance implications of PCIe and high-speed parallel CRC implementations. According to the evaluation results, the overall power consumption is reduced by 38% to 85%. The proposed method in this study is universal and can be used to optimize the energy efficiency of other similar CRC calculation alaorithms in the literature.

articleTitle: IMMA Performance in Uplink UAV Communications Over Rician Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper thoroughly explores the average bit error rate (ABER) performance of the index modulation multiple access (IMMA) technique in the realm of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication. It considers a range of channel conditions and varying altitudes of aerial base station (ABS). IMMA, recognized as a promising multiple access technique for uplink communication, showcases substantial enhancements in both user fairness and spectral efficiency. Employing extensive simulations, we meticulously analyze how key parameters, such as the Rician <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> - factor and small-scale fading models, impact the ABER performance. We leverage channel singular value de-composition (SVD) to gain deeper insights. The reported findings emphasize that IMMA adeptly mitigates challenges associated with non line-of -sight (NLOS) propagation in UAV scenarios, thereby achieving superior communication reliability compared to traditional techniques. These discoveries shed light on the practical deployment potential of IMMA in UAV communication networks, establishing a robust foundation for dependable and efficient uplink connectivity across diverse aerial environments.

articleTitle: A Predictive Maintenance Approach for Non-Effectively Earthed Radial Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Earth faults are the most common fault types in distribution networks. Earth faults can be permanent or incipient faults. Although incipient faults are temporary, they are prone to be turned into permanent faults depending on the insulation level of the system which leads severe impact on system safety. Therefore, incipient faults must be detected. Further, feeders with temporary faults should be evaluated to identify and rank the risky feeders. For this purpose, a hybrid-sequence-based trace algorithm is proposed for detecting faulted sections using COMTRADE data. The proposed method has been applied to the actual network in the European side of metropolitan Istanbul. Using the proposed approach, predictive maintenance is ensured for the distribution feeders.

articleTitle: Rate Regions of Two-Way Wireless Communication with Wireless Power Transfer under Different Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper investigates the achievable rate regions of wirelessly powered two-way communication employing wireless power transfer (WPT) between two users, facilitated by either a fixed or a mobile relay. The analysis encompasses several factors, beginning with an examination of the impact of enabling energy harvesting on achievable rates with a fixed relay, considering diverse transmission distances and varying the number of relay antennas. The study also explores the unique scenario of direct communication between the two users. Additionally, the paper investigates the influence of mobile relay trajectories and velocity on the achievable rate region. Results demonstrate significant variations in achievable rates based on these factors. The findings offer valuable insights, paving the way for future research endeavors.

articleTitle: Design of a USB Based Interface Adapter for the Verification of MIL-STD-1553 Compliant Avionic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In the realm of avionics hardware design verification, there arises a critical need for robust hardware and software infrastructure to conduct functional tests effectively. The MIL-STD-1553 standard simplifies data transfer between sensors, computers, indicators, and other aircraft equipment, enhancing electromagnetic compatibility, reliability, and fault tolerance of subsystems. However, the current state of access methods reveals the inherent challenges posed by their bulky and user-unfriendly hardware interface. To address these challenges, in this work, we propose a USB-based interface adapter for the MIL-STD-1553 bus. This innovative hardware interface uses USB technology to provide a compact and efficient means of connecting to the bus, making it more user-friendly and efficient for both development and debugging purposes. The portable nature of the USB-1553 adapter offers significant advantages, allowing for flexible deployment in various environments as well as eliminating the need to procure specialized instruments for automated testing, thus allowing cost savings and resource optimization. Our design rationale was further validated through experimental testing of the proposed design. Overall, the USB-1553 adapter enables efficiency, versatility, and cost-effectiveness for the factory and field level avionics design verification tasks.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Pre-Heating on Performance Enhancement of Li-ion Batteries in Aviation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this study, the effects of pre-heating in terms of the voltage and current capacities and performance parameters of the lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are investigated experimentally. The test setup includes resistive DC load banks, electrical isolation, and protection equipment, qualified Li-ion batteries for aviation, and data acquisition system. Load banks are utilized for supplying different ranks of resistive loads to the equipment under test through the protection devices. The Li-ion batteries are discharged with 10C, 12.5C, and 15C during the test activities, and the performance parameters are inspected by using a data acquisition system that includes the Aeronautical Radio, Incorporated (ARINC), and resistive temperature detector (RTD) modules by real-time monitoring and post data. These discharge test activities are reiterated for diverse temperatures for both operating with or without internal heater. The variety of the battery performance was illustrated in distinct State of Charge (SoC), and temperature values in this paper. It was seen that the internal heater directly affects the discharge performance of the Ii-ion battery.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling of a 2-kW Solid Oxide Fuel Cell System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study presents a model of 2-kW Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC) power system with auxiliary components. The system model encompasses an SOFC stack, two heat exchangers, a heater, a combustor, and stream divider modules. Nonlinear models including thermal, electrochemical, and voltage dynamics were developed and tested with variable electrical loads. When the stack is heated to a particular temperature using an electric heater, an electric current is applied to generate power. The voltage behavior of the stack is demonstrated with a polarization curve. The analysis also covers the cell potential and voltage drops in an individual cell along the limiting current capacity. There is a brief mention of the heating strategy, and the simulation results are presented at the end. We believe that the modeling approach contributes to systems engineering by giving insight before system design, and pretesting opportunity before system setup.

articleTitle: Development of Plastic Melter with Automated Conveying System and Temperature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In the Philippines, many industries produce single-use plastic, like plastic bottles for drinking, sachets, etc. They use single-use plastic because they can mass produce their products and they can make their own products into sachets, which can be cheaper than buying them in a big bottle. According to an article on the World Bank Website, the Philippines produces an estimated 2.7 million tons of plastic waste each year. Thus, the development a plastic melter that used rice husk as a fuel with an automated conveying system and temperature control is essential. The melter will utilize the rice husk as its fuel to melt the plastic and will control the temperature to avoid reaching the flash point of the plastic. The major parts of the Plastic Melter are as follows: furnace assembly, conveyor assembly, and automation system. Test results showed that the initial temperature inside the ladle was 31.5 °C. The starting temperature at the second test is 190.1 DC. The melting temperature ranges from 306°C to 340 °C. The average melting temperature is 316.8 °C. The melting time of shredded PET, LDPE, and HDPE ranges from 6.03 to 8.47 minutes, and the average melting time is 6.53 minutes. Thus, the rice husk combustion efficiency of the prototype is 20.68%, which melts 500 grams of shredded PET, HDPE, and LDPE.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Palestinian Mobile Networks Based on Crowdsourcing Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The evaluation of mobile network performance involves assessing various key performance indicators (KPIs) that gauge the efficiency and effectiveness of these networks. The key performance indicators of the Palestinian mobile networks are usually monitored by the mobile network operators (MNOs) through their operation support subsystems and the carried-out drive tests. This include the received signal level, received signal quality, drop rate, handover success rate, packet loss, latency, throughput, etc. The Palestinian ministry of telecommunications and information technology (MTIT) together with the Palestinian Telecom Regulatory Authority (PTRA) also conduct performance measurements for the mobile networks through drive tests to monitor the quality of service (QoS) measurements delivered by each mobile operator and compare them with the standard KPIs benchmark limits. They aim to enhance user experience and network efficiency. However, these performance measurements either from the MNOs or the regulation agency are limited and do not reflect the exact end user experience. Therefore, in this paper, we address the performance evaluation of the Palestinian MNOs based on a large community of connected people smartphone crowdsourcing technique. Here, using smartphone crowdsourcing can collect continuous real-time data on network performance from a large number of smartphone users with various locations. Thus, the quality of experience (QoE) can be evaluated from the end user perspective with a bigger data set. In this paper, we have developed and implemented a smartphone application called “Signal Sense” for crowdsourced mobile network measurements. The performed measurements include location information, signal level, signal quality and throughput for 3G mobile networks in Palestine. The evaluation of these measurements reflects the relative performance of the Palestinian MNOs.

articleTitle: PV-Based Electricity Production and Storage in Marine Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The energy required by marine vessels worldwide is mostly provided by using fossil fuels. Due to the depletion of fossil fuels day by day., causing environmental pollution and climate change., various measures have been taken in this direction worldwide., including the search for alternative solutions in marine vehicles. The need for environmentally friendly., economical and clean energy has accelerated the energy production in marine vessels with Renewable Energy Sources (RES). Solar energy., which is one of the RES., is one of the most preferred resources to be used among the RES because it is accessible everywhere in the world. In this study., Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) method is used to predict the solar radiation values in a region whose borders are determined on the Marmara Sea. PV power system modeling was created using the HOMER program on a marine vessel modeled with the values obtained from ANN., and technical and economic analysis of the electrical energy generation and storage of the marine vessel during the year was carried out and recommendations were presented. In this way., it has been tried to bring a new approach to electricity generation by maximizing the benefit of solar radiation in moving marine vehicles.

articleTitle: Optimal Distributed Generation Location to Reduce Energy Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The high demand for electricity worldwide has caused great interest in Distributed Generation (DG), as it is an aspect that can be used in rural areas, where the existence of water resources for centralized generation is scarce, thus trying to minimize electricity losses. It is one of the main problems addressed by the electricity system, factors that are subject to a number of parameters and variables that affect the efficiency of the grid in different ways. The location of distributed generation is vitally important as poor GD positioning increases the rate of losses. For the analysis of results, a first case study is evaluated, which does not contain the introduction of a Distributed Generation and another case that does. This document describes a distributed generation system with an installed capacity of 2.3 MW, which corresponds to case 2. Using the Neplan software, the objective is to analyze the losses obtained in the system in order to propose an improvement solution; thus, managing to reduce electrical disturbances in the system through optimization techniques, which have as a principle to provide a solution to the current problem using the IEEE 14-bar test system.

articleTitle: MCP Joints Estimation using EMG Signals and Elastic-Net Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Experiencing the loss of a hand, whether due to accidents or diseases, can significantly impact an individual's quality of life. Therefore, it is crucial to develop a continuous control mechanism capable of effectively controlling prosthetic devices with a substantial number of degrees of freedom, to replicate the intricate movements of the hand. This study investigates the feasibility of estimating metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint angles using electromyography (EMG) signals. Specifically, a set of features was extracted from the sEMG signals and utilized to construct an elastic-net regression model. The effectiveness of our approach was assessed using the publicly accessible NINAPRO sEMG dataset. The experimental results highlight the precision and continuity achieved by our approach in estimating the hand's MCP joint angles. The highest average coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R^{2})$</tex> across subjects for all movements reached 0.79, while the average <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> values computed for different MCP movements ranged from 0.70 to 0.95.

articleTitle: CRISP - DM Process in Smart Building Management
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Smart Buildings are buildings that integrate and combine intelligence, management, control, materials, and construction as a single system to meet all the needs of the building, such as comfort, energy efficiency, and durability. In universities, laboratories are used less frequently than other facilities and classrooms. Courses and students may change in the same classroom, and the period of use of such classrooms is much more extended than in laboratories. However, classrooms may only be used for classes during long breaks or for short periods of non-use between exams. In addition, there is no provision for when the heating system will start to heat up before classes or when it will be turned off after classes. By planning heating and lightning, energy and costs will be saved. This paper presents data acquisition methods for preparing a dataset to create a machine learning (ML) model to save energy loss in university laboratories. The developed model will predict energy consumption in classrooms and laboratories based on weather conditions. The study is being conducted in two stages. The first stage describes how to collect data using electronic devices such as Internet of Things (IoT) controllers of Smart Building Management Systems. The second stage gave possibilities for data analysis and preparation using the phases of the Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM).

articleTitle: Distributed Connected Dominating Set Based Algorithm for Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Ad-hoc networks are a communication protocol used in various sectors, particularly in military technologies. Unlike traditional network structures, Ad-hoc networks operate on the principle of peer-to-peer communication. Since the nodes within the network are not connected to a cellular infrastructure, distributed algorithms are required for the communication of nodes. However, it is important to carefully design these distributed algorithms based on essential criteria due to the challenges associated with ad-hoc networks. These criterias are considered to be particularly important when dealing with dynamically variable networks, such as a mobile ad-hoc networks. Mobile ad-hoc networks face significant challenges related to scaling, energy consumption, and stability. To address these challenges, various clustering algorithms employed, each with its own benefits and costs. In this study, a connected dominating set algorithm is proposed for mobile ad hoc networks, which can provide workload balance and protect the backbone structure relatively against mobility and can be an alternative solution to the congestion occurring on a single backbone by creating multiple backbone structures.

articleTitle: Investigation of Capacitive-Based Dust Sensor with Nanowires Sensing Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Dust particles represent a great challenge in dusty environments due to their accumulation on solar panels which drastically reduces their efficiency. Regular monitoring and cleaning based on dust sensor readings help maintaining the optimal solar panel performance and maximize energy production. However, current dust sensors are based on light scattering, with limitations including bulky size and high power consumption. In this work, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Fe}2\mathrm{O}_{3}, \text{ZnO}, \text{TiO}_{2}, \text{SnO}_{2}, \text{GaN}, \text{InAs},\text{CuO}, \text{SiC}, \mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{5}$</tex>, and CdSe nanowires are explored to be used as a capacitive-based sensing layer for dust sensors. Based on extensive simulations using COMSOL and SPICE softwares, ZnO nanowires show a high sensitivity of 7.77<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> when 25% of the sensor area is covered with dust, and 40.63% when 50% is covered with dust. The sensor capacitance increases from 80 pF to 130 pF as dust particles continue trapping within the spacing between the wires. The change in the capacitance is converted into voltage, where almost 1.2 V is obtained using a readout circuit implemented using a Wheatstone bridge, an instrumentation amplifier, and a full-wave rectifier. Utilizing nanostructures such as nanowires to detect dust levels in outdoor environments has applications in optimizing solar panel performance.

articleTitle: Bayesian Network Model for Cardiovascular Diseases Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In the last few arrays, cardiovascular disorders are a major concern for global health. The prevalence of these heart conditions is constantly increasing, posing a significant challenge for healthcare systems worldwide. Considering this reality, our work aims to develop a precise and reliable diagnostic tool that is essential for effectively detecting these disorders. In this paper, we propose a hybrid approach that combines two processing methods. The first method involves symlet-4 wavelet analysis, while the second method utilizes modeling through a naive Bayesian network. The objective of this work is to detect cardiovascular disorders from ECG signals and determine the classes of arrhythmias present, distinguishing them from normal ones. Our method has shown promising results and will contribute to improving the management of patients with cardiovascular disorders while reducing potential complications associated with these serious conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Critical Conduction Mode Boost PFC Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, PFC boost converter with CRM based on constant on-time current mode control is proposed. The proposed converter is analyzed and designed for 140 V- 275 V AC input voltages, 396 V output voltage and 410 W output power. Circuit parameters and components have been calculated and to verify the analyses, the converter is simulated with PSIM simulation program under 140 V worst condition and 220 V nominal voltage conditions. The simulation results show that calculated parameters are in accordance with analyzed and calculated results and increased power factor up to almost unity with EMI filter.

articleTitle: Novel Non-Linear Optimized Control Techniques for Conversion of Hybrid Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and reliable energy sources has spurred significant interest in renewable energy systems. The paper introduces a novel design for a grid-connected hybrid renewable energy system, integrating a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) wind turbine and a solar photovoltaic (PV) conversion system. The core focus is enhancing energy conversion efficiency using advanced components, including inverters and rectifiers. A significant contribution of this work is the application of the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, which optimises solar power output and wind speed, ensuring maximal energy extraction from both wind and solar sources. Furthermore, the paper presents innovative control techniques tailored to the nonlinear model of the converter-generator system. These techniques are pivotal in achieving the dual objectives of maximising energy conversion efficiency and ensuring system stability. The robustness and strength of the proposed approach are rigorously analysed using backstepping control methods and Lyapunov theory. The results of this analysis confirm the effectiveness and high efficiency of the proposed control strategy. This research contributes to the field of renewable energy by providing a more efficient and stable approach to hybrid energy conversion, which is vital for advancing sustainable and reliable energy systems.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network and Its Benefit in Modeling and Efficient Yield Analysis of Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents yield-aware antenna sizing and modelling through artificial neural network (ANN) leading to an accurate and efficient synthesis process. In the proposed methodology, the suitable amount of data is provided and then Quicksort algorithm is employed for categorizing the most/least effectiveness of each parameter. Finally, the ANN is trained and used for optimizing the design parameters leading to find optimal output specifications. The performance is named as yield analysis, and it accelerates in predicting the effects of variations in the antenna's dimension and it leads to find the optimal design parameters in a shortest time without any further simulation effort. The developed process results in accurate yield predictions of antenna dimensions with reduced time. To validate the efficiency of the proposed method, three antennas from the recently published literature are considered, and then our presented method is employed for optimizing them and quantify the computational time in modelling. The simulation results demonstrate that using the proposed method, there is approximately 25% speed-up in modelling, sizing, and optimizing antennas.

articleTitle: Design and Prototype Production of an Axial Displacement Measurement System by Using LVDT for Propeller Shaft Development Process
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Propeller shafts are responsible to transmit torque and rotational movement from an engine to related equipment. In addition, propeller shafts compensate axial and angular movement. Various data are acquired on propeller shafts in real-time because it is dynamic and challenging working conditions. These data provide health monitoring opportunity and information about propeller shaft. Also, these data are used for product design and development process. Data acquisition on propeller shafts is one of the most important subjects for design issue. There is a demand to acquire data like temperature, stress or displacement which sustain functionality. Propeller shaft's sliding part that compensates the axial movement is a special example for this data acquisition need. In this paper, it is focused on how to measure axial displacement on a propeller shaft during field and rig tests. A linear variable differential transformer (LVDT) sensor was designed to detect the axial movement in the slip assembly of the propeller shaft. A signal conditioner circuit was built with AD598 for the signal processing. The system prototype was produced and tested. The sensor measurement range was optimized according to propeller shaft's slip assembly travel distance.

articleTitle: Design Improvements with Temperature-Rise Tests and Analysis in Disconnectors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In medium and high-voltage systems, disconnectors are switchgear devices that can open and close when the circuit is unloaded and create a visible separation gap in the open position. One of the most critical tests performed on disconnectors is the temperature-rise test. The requirements of the EC 62271–1 standard are met during the application of this test on load-switching disconnectors. This study examines the temperature-rise test results of these disconnectors, which can operate up to 2500A rated voltage currents at 36 kV rated voltage level for up to 480 minutes. This study reveals how the temperature-rise tests are performed and the design improvements made to pass this test.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Comfort of Modern Buildings Considering Energy Conservation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In December 2002, the “Directive on the Energy Performance of Buildings” was endorsed by European countries. EU member nations are mandated to integrate this directive into their national legislation promptly, considering the minimum energy efficiency standards for buildings. The Directive comprises two main documents: Document 1- “Final Energy Consumption” and Document 2 - “Energy Consumption in Residential Buildings across EU nations.” Implementing this Directive necessitates the formulation of a comprehensive standard with updated criteria for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems. The ultimate outcome of this Directive aims at certifying the energy efficiency of both existing and new constructions. Given that Azerbaijan has not yet adopted laws on energy efficiency, resulting in a lack of actual building certifications for both older and newer structures, absence of energy audits in the construction industry, and an unidentified potential for unused energy resources, notably thermal energy, it is clear that substantial work lies ahead in this area.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral Unmixing Using Nonconvex Shrinkage and Total Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Sparse hyperspectral unmixing aims to estimate the abundance map in the presence of a large spectral library. We propose an nonconvex shrinkage and total variation based sparse hyperspectral unmixing method. Since abundance matrix has a sparse structure naturally, nonconvex shrinkage function in the proposed formulation is used to obtain a sparse solution instead of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_1$</tex> norm which is used generally in sparse regression problems. Moreover, abundance map has a piecewise smooth which means that neighboring pixels have similar spatial structure, total variation is employed in the formulation to satisfy the abundance map homogeneity by smoothing it. The proposed formulation is solved by splitting the optimization problem using alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Although the proposed formulation is nonconvex, ADMM solution is able to obtain the solution. The proposed method is good at estimating the abundance map and performs well compared to competitive methods in the literature.

articleTitle: An Islanded DC Microgrid Blueprint for Residential Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Rising energy demands and unsustainable practices necessitate innovative solutions. Motivated by a middle-class family's requirements, the system makes use of solar energy that is efficiently handled via a DC-DC converter and harvested by photovoltaic panels. This paper presents the design of an island DC microgrid specifically tailored for residential applications. A battery storage system with optimized charging and discharging capabilities ensures power availability, even during grid outages. Stable voltage regulation within the microgrid is achieved through a current-controlled PID controller. The system incorporates a mix of constant power loads to optimize energy utilization. This detailed design offers a sustainable and reliable residential power solution, paving the way for wider adoption of DC microgrids and a greener future.

articleTitle: Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA) Optimized PI-Controller for Modular Multi-Level Converter Based HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Nowadays, Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) technology becomes widespread to interconnect different energy grids in High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission systems. However, it is relatively new technology that needs to improve active and reactive power flow controls in order to reduce voltage deviations and also increase robustness of the overall system performance against the faults. This study is related to the specified control problem of the MMC based HVDC systems. In this study, PI-controllers used in internal current control, DC voltage control, and active and reactive power controls of MMC based HVDC power transmission system is adjusted simultaneously with the A sine-cosine algorithm as a powerful heuristic method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fixed and Single-Axis Tracking Systems in Solar Power Plants: A Case Study for Kırıkkale Province in Turkey
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study examines resources used in response to today's increasing energy demands. Considering fossil fuels' limited availability and environmental harm, the need for renewable, clean energy is steadily growing. Among these clean energy sources, the most popular is solar energy, which reduces carbon emissions and is also a renewable resource. After analyzing our country's solar energy potential, the solar radiation value for the Kirikkale province has been evaluated. Subsequently, solar power plants with fixed and tracking-axis systems to be installed in the same region for Kirikkale province are studied using the PVsyst program version 7.4.2, and the production data obtained are compared. The comparison of these results and the obtained data can be conducted using up-to-date information for different countries and provinces as well.

articleTitle: Developing a Multifunctional Electronic Control Board and Customizing it for the Irrigation of Large Area Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The rapid increase in the world's population is leading to a significant rise in global water demand. This growth has further exacerbated the challenges of sustainable water management by increasing the need for water resources. As a solution to promote water conservation and effective water usage, a deep learning-based irrigation system has been designed, with a multifunctional electronic control card developed as a key component of this holistic system. The multifunctional electronic control card is tasked with real-time data collection from the field, transferring this data to a workstation where deep learning algorithms operate via the internet, and also overseeing the outputs generated by the deep learning algorithms at the central workstation that need to be executed in the field by the controlled peripheral equipment. Additionally, the arrangement and operation of this peripheral equipment are managed by the electronic card. In areas with large surface areas such as golf courses, where the throw distances of sprinklers are fixed, narrowing the irrigation area is ineffective. By customizing the system through the control of irrigation pump speeds by the electronic card, based on the quantity and direction determined by the deep learning algorithms, the system aims to optimize water usage, thereby increasing water conservation and irrigation efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Highly Efficient Microwave Absorber for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study presents the design of a highly efficient microwave absorber on an FR-4 substrate measuring 48x66x1.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. Design and simulation were conducted using CST STUDIO, with several parametric studies aimed at achieving increased absorption within the desired frequency band. Alterations to the geometric shape constituted the stages of absorber refinement, with simulation values analyzed to assess absorber efficiency at each stage. Throughout the four analysis steps, the absorption was obtained at three different frequency values covering the n77 and n78 5G bands, with the highest absorption observed at 3.8 GHz. In conclusion, in the final geometric configuration, electromagnetic wave absorption percentages were determined as 97.3%, 98.04%, and 97.8% at frequencies of 3.7 GHz, 3.8 GHz, and 3.9 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Developement of 4-Ports MIMO CP Antennas for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper introduces a printed four-port MIMO antenna with advantages such as compact size, excellent MIMO diversity performance, and simple geometry for radar applications at 10 GHz. It is small size makes it suitable for integrating various telecommunication devices for multiple applications, with a prototype measuring 32 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 32$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4.3$</tex> mm. The mutual coupling between the individual elements significantly im-pacts the MIMO system's diversity properties, and an effective technique of orthogonally positioning the antenna elements to each other increases their isolation resulting in superior MIMO diversity performance. It is evaluated through S-parameters and MIMO diversity parameters to ensure its suitability for future radar applications. It is validated through measurements, and the results showed a good match between simulated and measured results. The different diversity parameters such as (Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), Diversity Gain (DG), Channel Capacity Loss (CCL), Multiplexing Efficiency (ME), Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) are simulated and measured. It is found that all values are within the standard norms which indicates the availability for MIMO radar applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems: A Comparative Study using Whale Optimization Algorithm and Hawks Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a pivotal role in safeguarding computer networks against malicious activities. This research explores the efficacy of two optimization algorithms, namely Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) and Hawks Optimization (HHO), for feature selection to enhance the performance of IDS. The NSL-KDD dataset is utilized as a benchmark to evaluate the impact of selected features on classification accuracy. The study employs the Random Forest (RF) classification algorithm to evaluate the effectiveness of feature selection methods. Implementation is conducted in Python, leveraging its versatile libraries and frameworks. Comparative analysis reveals that when integrating the selected features, RF attains superior results compared to utilizing features separately for binary and multiclass classifications. Results indicate that RF with HHO achieves an impressive accuracy of 98.02%, showcasing the prowess of HHO in enhancing IDS performance. Meanwhile, RF with WOA achieves a commendable accuracy of 97.81%.

articleTitle: Power and Temperature Investigation for High-Resolution Atomic Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Nowadays, quantum-based sensor research is one of the most fascinating and popular areas of study. High-resolution laser spectroscopy is the basis of high-sensitive atomic magnetometer, gyroscope, and clock technologies that work according to the principle of laser-atom interaction. For this reason, the atomic transitions of the D2 line of the Cs alkali metal were examined with a specially manufactured atomic vapor cell. In this context, atomic transitions at different powers and temperatures have been reported. Thus, it is aimed to investigate parameters such as linewidth, etc. with high-resolution spectroscopy techniques to improve sensor sensitivities in spectroscopy-based applications.

articleTitle: System of System Architecture for Cybersecurity of Power Systems Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Smart grids are at risk of cyber-attacks due to more connected devices being introduced. Different kinds of attacks may incur different consequences in the operation of smart grids. Attackers have identified different vulnerable points in smart grid operations and have developed malicious stealthy attacks to disrupt the operation of physical systems. In this paper we have formulated the power system cyber security problem as a five-dimensional optimization problem. A general framework is developed using the system of system explorer tool providing a defensive solution to the vulnerable points of a smart grid prone to malicious attacks. An optimal meta-architecture composed of defensive system constituents is achieved using Genetic algorithm (GA) and fuzzy inference system providing a solution to ensure cybersecurity of power system operations.

articleTitle: Realistic Sonar Image Generation With Rendering Method for Underwater Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Underwater object detection is used for search operations, structure examinations, underwater navigation and archaeological site investigation. Underwater object detection algorithms need high resolution sonar image dataset in order to use this dataset to train their algorithms for accurate detection. Sonar image dataset can be obtained by using side scan sonar. However, acquisition of sonar images from sonar systems is costly and time-consuming due to harsh environmental conditions and also, the low resolution of sonar images creates problems while training object detection algorithms. This paper presents an efficient method which generates realistic sonar image dataset with different backgrounds to train object detection algorithms using rendering method. In this method, in order to generate realistic sonar image dataset; firstly, objects (ship and airplane) are rendered on different axes. Then, by changing the background of the image and adding shadow and noise, realistic sonar image dataset is created in a fast and less costly way. Finally, this realistic sonar image dataset is used to train You Look Only Once (YOLO) object detection algorithm. After training of the detection algorithm by rendering method, real wrecked plane and ship sonar images taken from side scan sonar are detected successfully.

articleTitle: 3D Printing of Electrically Conductive Carbon-Based Composites for Flexible Strain Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental method of fused deposition modeling FDM 3D printing (3DP) technology. A combination of electrically conductive filaments with an encapsulate insulating substrate was possible to be simultaneously 3D printed using a dual extrusion 3D printer. The electrical and mechanical properties of the 3D-printed samples were explored throughout this paper. We investigated the viability of carbon-filled polymer composites for the potential to sense strain deformations. Carbon black and carbon nanotubes proved to be excellent conducting fillers to the thermoplastic polyurethane polymer matrix and be used as flexible filaments for strain-sensing applications.

articleTitle: Optimizing Control of Railway Traction Motor Performance with a Hardware-in-the-Loop Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study investigates the implementation of an advanced control strategy, field-oriented control (FOC), to optimize the performance of a railway traction motor within a hardware-in-the Loop (HIL) environment. The HIL setup, facilitated by the Texas Instrument (TI) C2000 micro controller unit (MCU) and Plecs RT Box 3 simulator, serves as a robust testing ground that allows real-time simulation and validation of the proposed FOC algorithm under varying loads and dynamic conditions. The methodology involves integrating the FOC algorithm into the MCU and models of the three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) and traction motor into the RT Box 3 simulator. With a 1000V DC supply and a 1 kHz switching frequency suitable for rail vehicle systems, an effective and quite precise torque control was achieved with a peak-to-peak deviation of 10% from the reference torque value on the alternating current (AC) induction motor, which is one of the most preferred motor types in trains.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal Polymer Bandpass Filter with UWB Performance Using Cascaded Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The suggested design introduces a unique bandpass filter that utilizes Marchand balun to achieve ultra-wideband (UWB) performance. Due to the varying input/output impedances of the planar Marchand balun, the UWB bandpass filter can be adjusted to have a varying fractional bandwidth. This is achieved by connecting two planar Marchand baluns in series, utilizing the principles of transversal filter ideas and multilayer LCP technology. Comprehensive instructions for the design and synthesis of the UWB bandpass filter are included.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Antenna for Automotive Applications at 76.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna candidate for automotive cars and MIMO radar applications. It is implemented on Rogers RO4003C with a relative dielectric constant of 3.55 and a thickness of 0.203 mm. Linearly and circularly polarized versions of printed antennas are presented and operate at 76.5 GHz, which meets the characteristics of the required application. One of the antennas is selected and fabricated for validation. The results of the reflection coefficient fo und good agreement between the simulated and measured ones. Further antenna parameters like 3D and 2D radiation patterns, realized gain and axial ratio are illustrated.

articleTitle: Wireless Body Area Network Authentication Using Lightweight Security Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The advancement of wireless communication, Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) has gained a lot of attention with the development of compact sensors Medical information is very sensitive. If any physiological information is tampered with or intercepted. It may affect the diagnosis or the patient's privacy. Security in WBAN is still important. Therefore, it is important to verify the authentication of each other's sending and receiving data between the sensor node and the server to protect patient information from malicious people, and for the privacy of patients. This research presents a protocol for secure authentication between sensor node and server nodes connected to the patient's body. We use the hash function and symmetric encryption to make the lightweight protocol.

articleTitle: Utilization of a Shooting and Bouncing Ray Method to Estimate the VOR Systems Bearing Error
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: When man-made or natural obstacles are located close to radio-navigation systems, it becomes imperative to assess their electromagnetic impacts on pre-existing radio-navigation installations. This paper introduces a shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method scheme for computing electromagnetic scattering from electrically large, lossy and complex objects when excited by near-field sources such as infinitesimal dipole sources. Example scattering scenarios for validation are explained, and bearing error estimation results are presented for a very high-frequency omnidirectional radio (VOR) system which is one of the most common radio-navigation aids.

articleTitle: Comparative Design Analysis of a 1 MW Islanded and Non-Islanded Floating Solar Power System at Mangla Hydro Reservoir
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Solar energy is increasingly recognised as an essential part of the global mission for the net zero goal, owing to its renewable nature and cost-effectiveness. In response to escalating power demands, private power operators and industrial investors seek ways to mitigate electricity costs. This study addresses a specific project: an industrial tender for a 1-megawatt hybrid floating solar power plant intended for a water purification industry in Pakistan. The sector has varying monthly load requirements based on product utilisation and aims to sell surplus energy back to the grid after meeting its operational demands. The choice of a floating solar power plant is driven by the prohibitively high land costs in the vicinity of the dam in Islamnagar, Azad Kashmir, coupled with the unfeasibility of meeting industrial water requirements at locations distant from the dam. This paper will conduct a comparative analysis of grid-connected and standalone options for this industry, focusing on performance metrics. The optimal system, characterised by high efficiency and minimal loss, will be selected for the solar plant design. This design will address aspects including load management, battery storage, and energy provision to the grid.

articleTitle: Development of a Split Ring Resonator Sensor for Vibration Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The main focus of this work is the development of a metamaterial-based vibration sensor for the detection of earthquake amplitudes. The sensor is composed of two metamaterial layers made of FR-4 substrates with Circular Split Ring Resonators (CSRR) arranged in a back-to-back configuration on each substrate. The variation of the spacing between the plates results in an alteration of the electric field and thus changes in the resonance frequencies of the whole system.
