The system is designed and optimized to resonate in the GSM 1.8 GHz band, which ultimately results in a self-sustaining sensor. A clear relationship between the spacing of the two layers and the shift in the resonance frequency has been obtained. It also changes the magnitude of the reflected and absorbed energy from the sensor. This spacing in turn can be directly correlated with the vibration amplitudes. The system can be integrated into a warning system with the ability to quantify the structural resilience of buildings against potentially damaging vibrations. Different unit cell geometries of metamaterial surface are tested before selecting the CSRR geometry to develop highly sensitive sensors operating in the GSM frequency band at 1.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Determination of Transformer Operating Condition with Different Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: When diagnosing the condition of transformers, classification is generally made into normal and faulty states. However, in some cases, an increase in the amount of hydrogen and hydrocarbons in the insulating oil is observed even if there is no malfunction. This situation is called stray gassing. Ignoring stray gassing may lead to misdiagnosis. In this study, real transformer data have been classified as normal state, faulty state and stray gassing. First, real data has been labeled with gas percentages using the Duval Pentagon 1 method. Then, two data sets have been created, consist of 5 gas and 9 gas concentrations. Transformer condition diagnosis has been made using the classification algorithms Fine Tree, Linear SVM, Bagging Trees and Subspace KNN for the raw data set and pre-processed data, and the results have been compared. In addition to using different gases to increase diagnostic performance, the data has pre-processed and analyzed. The highest diagnostic accuracy has been achieved with the pre-processed version of Dataset-2, which contains 9 gas data with a large number of features.

articleTitle: Adaptive Dynamic Tariff Factor for Distribution Network Congestion Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Network congestion is the main problem in the distribution system. It is necessary to study dynamic tariff methods to curtail network congestion problems. Through the use of dynamic tariffs, regulatory prices have the potential to be either positive (tariff) or negative (subsidy). To address these challenges, stakeholders have implemented different types of tariffs, making iterative adjustments in pricing and/or engaging in contractual arrangements driven by incentives. However, dynamic tariffs cannot handle a large number of distribution energy resources. Here we show this research to determine the dynamic tariff using two calculation methods (line constraint and baseline load). The adaptive dynamic tariff factor has been used to adjust the price of electricity via real data recorded from a five-feeder distribution network. The results demonstrated that the line constraint method can reduce electricity prices up to 28.16% and increase electricity prices by 37.25%, providing an incentive for consumers to change their schedule and reduce the congestion problem.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive and Cost-Effective Monitoring of Street Lighting Photometric Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The United Arab Emirates has a large and sophisticated street lighting infrastructure; therefore, the photometric performance of the street lighting systems must be prioritized. Locating the malfunctions in a large street lighting infrastructure can be time-consuming and arduous. In this paper, a low-cost street lighting performance monitoring system is designed, implemented, and tested. The proposed system comprises three main components: an illuminance sensor, a spectrometer, and a GNSS receiver. These components build a light and robust system to mount on vehicles' rooftops. Additionally, a comprehensive data analysis and inference engine is developed to determine the photometric performance of the lighting poles by identifying the number and the position of the defective luminaires, under-performing luminaires, poles obstructed by vegetation, and lighting poles that suffer from a complete power outage due to electrical faults in lighting control cabinets. Lastly, the field survey results are demonstrated in reports and interactive online visualization using Google Maps, in which the obtained information can be converted into performance metrics and indexes overlayed on urban maps.

articleTitle: GNU Radio-Based SSK MIMO System: From Concept to Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The inherent characteristics of space shift keying (SSK) had generated substantial research interest in the domain of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, resulting in the development of hardware-based implementations. With the emergence of software-defined radio (SDR) technologies, radios could be implemented through software solutions. One prominent open-source SDR toolkit, GNU Radio, offered a comprehensive suite of signal processing blocks tailored for this purpose. In this study, a 2 × 2 SSK MIMO system was implemented using GNU Radio, inclusive of the deployment of advanced algorithms on a commercially available SDR platform for real-time transmission and reception. To assess the effectiveness of the implementation, meticulous comparisons were made between measurement results and simulation outcomes, revealing a high degree of accuracy in matching for a Rician fading channel characterized by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-factor of 2.5.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Energy Management Problem of a Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle Using Genetic Algorithm and Big-Bang Big-Crunch Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study is conducted on the modeling of a fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle (FCHEV) and the development of an optimization-based energy management strategy (EMS) based on the Big-Bang Big-Crunch (BBBC) algorithm and Genetic Algorithm (GA). GA is widely utilized in the literature as a global optimization method in EMS problems, however the BBBC algorithm is firstly used in an energy management study of a FCHEV. A quasi-static FCHEV model is designed to be a test platform in simulation to evaluate the BBBC-based and GA-based EMSs. Both strategies achieved a maximized fuel economy, and prolonged cycle life of the power sources. While the GA-based EMS improved the fuel economy and extended battery lifecycle, the BBBC-based EMS minimized degradation of the fuel cell with closely following the success of the GA-based EMS in fuel economy and prolonging the battery life. In general, the results have shown that BBBC has a potential to be used as an offline optimization method in benchmarking in this area.

articleTitle: Design of the Digital Control Block of an Analog Beamformer Suitable for Ultrasound Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: An analog beamformer for ultrasound receivers is designed at the system level, aiming for a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), a small chip area, and low power dissipation. The transducer structure used as the receiver has eight channels. The SUB-BF method was used in the analog beamformer structure to obtain a high SNR value. The control logic block, the most challenging part of the design, produces clocks with a fine delay resolution of 6.25 ns. The control logic block consists of a delay-locked loop, a duty cycle adjustment circuit, and a phase selector circuit. Clocks with 16 different delays generated by the delay-locked loop are sent to the phase selector circuit, and the selection process is performed according to the bit sequences sent by an external FPGA. All delay information was obtained using mathematical models with the support of the Matlab environment. 6.25 ns resolution and a maximum delay of 680 ns were acquired for this ABF using the parameters as the beam-steering angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex>, the carrier frequency of 2.5 MHz with a wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda_{\mathrm{c}})$</tex> of 600 µm, target area between 1 cm - 6 cm, and the distance between focal points of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{c}/8$</tex>.

articleTitle: Extended Kalman Filter Based Nonlinear Probabilistic Model Predictive Control of an Autonomous Motorcycle
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This work focuses on the control of a nonlinear autonomous motorcycle model using Probabilistic Model Predictive Control (MPC). The main purpose of this work is to control the speed, yaw angle and roll angle of the motorcycle while keeping its balance during a maneuver. The Probabilistic MPC takes into account the probabilistic disturbances acting on the control inputs or the state variables. The cost function of the optimization of this proposed nonlinear probabilistic MPC is different than the cost of traditional deterministic MPC, such that, it contains terms that represent the mean of the state variable which is calculated with the help of an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and also the terms as the functions of covariances of the state variables and control inputs. The optimization algorithm is fed with these mean and covariance values every time instant, then the controller calculates the optimal control sequence to apply it to the system model. The speed of the motorcycle, the yaw angle and, the roll angle of the motorcycle are controlled with good efficiency.

articleTitle: A Webbed Foot Design of Amphibious Quadruped Robot to Adapt Coastal Environment in Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The paper introduces an innovative webbed foot design for amphibious quadruped robots, aiming to address the challenges of traversing between water and land. Inspired by the natural locomotion of ducks, the robot's foot mechanism is engineered to provide efficient propulsion in water and stable locomotion on land. The design incorporates dual-hinged feet with a spring mechanism, enabling dynamic environmental adaptation. The study suggests that the webbed foot design offers a promising solution for amphibious locomotion, with potential for further advancements in whole-body control and underwater gait optimization. In the simulation environment, the system encompasses inverse kinematics for leg trajectory simulation, gait planning with cycloid tracks, and a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller for ankle adaptability. An analytical force model also accounts for granular media and fluid dynamics, enhancing the robot's performance in diverse conditions. Experimental trials, involving stability and velocity comparisons on inclined planes with and without sinusoidal forces, demonstrate the flipped robot's superior stability and comparable speed. Future work will focus on long-term durability testing and the development of more adaptive locomotion strategies.

articleTitle: The Enhancement of Power System Stability Using Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper is aimed at proposing a new adaptive controller to calculate the overall inertia in the system. The proposed controller estimates the sudden change in the load value that gives the required amount of inertia of the power system. The enhancement of the stability margins for the system is done by injecting virtual inertia to the system via the virtual synchronous generator. IEEE 9-bus system has been chosen for the verification of the proposed control. The effectiveness of the controller is verified by comparing the simulation results with the values for real data points. MATLAB® Simulink software is used for the simulations in this study. The results show that the virtual synchronous generator enhances the critical clearing time for the system by 14 ms compared to the normal inverter.

articleTitle: Modeling of a DC Motor and Position Angle Control Using Optimized PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Nowadays, DC (direct current) motors are widely used in industry. Air conditioners, computer drives, electric toothbrushes, portable vacuum cleaners, drilling machines, trimmers, food mixers are some areas where DC motors are used. Moreover, large DC motors are used in propulsion of electric vehicles, elevators, hoists, and in drives for steel rolling mills. Thus, controller design for DC motors is of great importance due to their widespread use. In this research, modeling of a DC motor and position angle controller design is explained. Optimum PID (proportional-integral-derivative) controller coefficients are obtained tuning the PID controller and thus a controller design with fast rise time, low overshoot, short settling time and no steady state error is achieved. The DC motor is modeled in both MATLAB and Simulink, simulations are realized with both of them and the same successful results are obtained.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Enhanced Trajectory Tracking with Multi-Obstacle Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this study, trajectory planning was conducted employing the Model Predictive Control (MPC) approach. This method predicts the future state variables of the system by utilizing a simplified vehicle model known as the bicycle model. These predicted state variables are used in generating future control signals. Initially, the traditional equations of vehicle dynamics were elucidated, and these equations were rederived. Subsequently, multiple static obstacles were introduced to ensure a collision-free path in the application of the MPC method. The simulation of this method is executed using MATLAB with the assistance of CasADi, referencing a trajectory tracking scenario. The optimization of objective criteria in the model was achieved through the Interior Point Optimization method. Upon incorporating velocity as an input using a nonlinear model, encountered results were explained, and challenges were addressed by employing acceleration as an input. Consequently, by reducing the input signal to acceleration, constraints on all states were implemented, enabling successful trajectory tracking. The outcomes of the proposed method in the simulation environment are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Between Transform-Based Deep Learning Approaches for ECG Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, we studied and compared the benefits of applying transformation as a preprocessing step to the input of the deep learning algorithms. A comparison was conducted between the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and fast Fourier transform (FFT) as feature extractors for the ECG signals. The generated feature vectors were fed to a convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) model for classification. Extensive experiments were executed on ECG signals collected from MIT-BIH and BIDMC databases with 3 classes. The obtained results showed the combined power of transformation and deep learning which led to better classification accuracies.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Differential Phase Shifter Based on Ferrite Loaded Rectangular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Phase shifters are passive microwave devices used in many communication systems. Phase shifters change the phase of the applied signal. In this way, phase shifters can be used to adjust the phase of the signal going to each antenna in phased array antenna systems, to perform beam scanning in radar applications. While ferrite phase shifters can be used as a stand-alone structure, they can also be used as a sub-system in circulator designs. In this study, nonreciprocal phase shifter analysis and 90-degree differential phase shifter structure are proposed for two different ferrite geometries and layouts. Proposed nonreciprocal phase shifter can be effectively used in the design of Differential Phase Shift Circulators.

articleTitle: A Study on Tennis Ball Ground Impact Point Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Due to the limitations of low-cost cameras in object tracking, it may be challenging to obtain reliable data from recordings captured by such cameras, particularly when dealing with moving objects. In this work, a novel technique was established to precisely identify and monitor the motions of the tennis ball and ground contact locations using low-resolution and low-frame-rate video recordings. The research paper presents a methodology that effectively identifies and monitors the rapid motions of a tennis ball, regardless of fluctuations in illumination and low frames per second values. By combining techniques for image enhancement, motion estimation, and adaptive filtering, the developed algorithm attempts to overcome the shortcomings of existing systems. Even under demanding conditions, the results of this study demonstrate that the algorithm achieves a high rate of success in detecting objects during sports analyses captured with low-resolution cameras. In summary, this study presents a novel approach to enhance precision and availability in the domains of sports science and performance analysis, particularly in settings with limited resources.

articleTitle: Lock-Up Clutch Adaptation for Automatic Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study includes functionality, working principle and actuation of lock-up clutch. Additionally, it investigates parameters that adversely affect clutch performance. To overcome the negative effects of these parameters, a dynamic adaptation method is developed. Some of system parameters are manipulated and adaptation on clutch for unexpected conditions are performed. This method ensures that target pressure profile is always tracked for different conditions. Any deviation between target and actual is observed by combining plant model and adaptation function in simulation environment. Results verify applicability of the approach.

articleTitle: Extraction of Fetal Electrocardiogram Utilizing BiLSTM Combined with FastICA
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) plays a crucial role in fetal monitoring. However, extraction of FECG from abdominal mixed signals is often affected by various noises and interferences, with maternal electrocardiogram (MECG) being the primary source of interference. Effectively suppressing the MECG component from the abdominal mixed signals presents a significant challenge. A hybrid model for FECG extraction is proposed by combining fast independent component analysis with adaptive noise cancellation method. In this approach, FastICA is used for thoracic electrocardiogram (TECG) estimation, and a bi-directional long short-term memory network acts as a non-linear adaptive filter for MECG suppression. The results of experiments on the PCDB and ADFECGDB database show that the proposed approach achieved good performance. The F1 score of proposed FECG extraction method is 99.36% on the NIFECGDB database and 98.48% on the PCDB database. The FastICA-BiLSTM model can be applied to intelligent devices for FECG analysis, facilitating the detection of anomalies in fetal monitoring and ensuring healthy childbirth by providing clinical information.

articleTitle: Fog Computing Service Placement Orchestrator
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Fog computing being an extension of cloud computing is meant to provide services at the edge of the network. It is expected to deal with the QoS problems which cloud computing cannot solve alone. One of the challenges in this heterogeneous device environment with a high mobility is an optimized service placement. Highly mobile end-devices and constantly changing fog node resources require distributed orchestration methods for optimized performance and resilience. We propose a service placement orchestrator model which is distributed across all the fog nodes for better resilience. It supports end-device mobility since end-devices can dynamically connect to fog nodes. And the service placement is optimized based on IMOPSO and AHP methods. As it is visible from the test results, currently a placement problem solving takes at least 50% of time in a powerful node such as PC, but it can slow down even more in a less powerful hardware. However, it is a fully functional solution in real-life conditions with up to 10 nodes and 30 services delivering a placement in almost 0.5 second.

articleTitle: TOA Localization Algorithm Based on Least Squares Method and LM Algorithm Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: A Time of Arrival (TOA) algorithm based on the signal arrival time from the neural network training method trainlm is proposed because different complicated indoor settings result in low positioning accuracy and diverse influencing factors. Additionally, simulation experiments were carried out based on the BP neural network algorithm in order to identify the model [1], and the trainlm training method was employed in order to lessen the influence of the surrounding environment, noise, and other factors on the outcomes. Following several trials, the data from the landing sites' densest areas were selected as performance evaluation indicators. Furthermore, the least squares method and trainlm are well-known and highly effective algorithms that can greatly increase localization accuracy. Additionally, research has shown that the technique is highly useful in a variety of settings.

articleTitle: A Robust Genetic Based Constraint Scheduling Algorithm to Promote On-Demand Cloud Services
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The scientific workflow scheduling provides an effective technique to improve cloud services performance and address the user constraints. However, many cloud services are limited in their execution time, storage, and cost, but few are anticipated to enhance workflow task scheduling based on certain quality of service constraints. This research presents a genetic algorithm for offline scheduling tasks with deadlines and budget constraints. The proposed approach utilizes the three-point crossover operation to generate better offspring. The proposed method is simulated in WorkflowSim and assessed using several state-of-the-art scientific workflows. The experimental results validate the competent performance of the proposed approach over well-known scheduling methods.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Decision Prediction in Turkish Legal Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Since text recognition studies in the literature are generally carried out in English, tokenization processes of Turkish legal texts in the Ural-Altaic language family cannot be used much. In this study, we tokenize Turkish legal texts and perform decision prediction using a deep learning Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. Artificial intelligence (AI), which is developing at a rapid pace, has become applicable to almost all fields of study and has started to be used effectively. Developments in AI have affected the field of law as well as other fields of study. The use and spread of AI in the field of law has increased significantly in recent years. One of the most important factors in this increase is that there is a huge amount of data in the field of law. It has become a need to analyze this data and transform it into meaningful and usable information. This paper aims to make decision prediction using artificial intelligence in judicial applications. In the study, using CNN, a neural network-based deep learning model, decision prediction was made with the data published by the Ombudsman's Office on the institution's website, which is free from publicly accessible personal data. The model was trained on the applicant information and the type of decision in the decision text. An F1 score of 0.63 was achieved for decision prediction.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Abnormal Tooth Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Federated learning has become a key method in medical research, not only for its effectiveness in handling sensitive data but also for enabling collaboration between different centers while ensuring patient privacy. This study aims to fill a research gap in the use of federated learning in dentistry, a field where the protection of sensitive data is crucial. We compare the performance of federated learning with local and central learning in dental disease detection. Our research focuses on two scenarios: one involving imbalanced data distribution across different centers, and another on continual learning, where the model's ability to learn new classes introduced by a single center is evaluated. Our results indicate that federated learning could be a promising approach, particularly when central learning is not feasible. The findings are especially encouraging in the continual learning scenario, suggesting that federated learning is adept at adapting to new information while maintaining previously acquired knowledge.

articleTitle: An Emulator of the Sea Surface Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The sea surface temperature is affected by the flow rate of seawater, salinity, and sea surface pressure. In ESGF, the global data from 1951 to 2014 can be filtered and merged to obtain the final dataset for machine learning. The training set occupies 500 of them and the rest is the testing set, which separately train and evaluate the model. By utilizing data such as seawater salinity, the flow rate of seawater, and sea surface pressure over a while, the model predicts changes in sea level temperature in the future. The final model is obtained with the best prediction performance. After that, the three variables the flow rate of seawater, salinity, and sea surface pressure have been analyzed, which affect temperature to see which one has the greatest impact on temperature. Our findings suggest that temperature is the most sensitive to changes in the flow rate of seawater, followed by salinity and sea surface pressure.

articleTitle: Sparse Recovery Using SL0 Algorithm by Dictionary Optimization and Application to ISAR Imaging with Low SNR
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging based on compressed sensing (CS) theory can recover complete information from limited ISAR echo signals and reduce the imaging cost of ISAR. The traditional Smooth L0 norm (SL0) algorithm can effectively solve the problem of ISAR signal recovery in the case of high SNR. However, there are usually strong noise and clutter in radar imaging, which greatly reduces the quality of ISAR signal recovery. On the basis of the traditional SL0 algorithm, this paper introduces the dictionary optimization process and proposes the dictionary optimization SL0 algorithm (DO-SL0). By optimizing the dictionary to adapt to the characteristics of the target signal, the performance of signal recovery is improved, the quality of sparse signal recovery under low SNR environment is improved while the cost is controlled, and the ISAR imaging results are effectively improved. In this paper, image entropy (ENT) is used to evaluate and compare ISAR images in low SNR environments using DO-SL0, SL0 and OMP methods respectively. Numerical experiment results show that under the same test conditions, the image entropy of sparse restored ISAR images using DO-SL0 method is lower than that of the other two methods, which verifies that the new algorithm can obtain higher quality restored signals in low SNR environment.

articleTitle: A Survey of Recent Optimization Techniques in Power Distribution Network Reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Optimizing the structure and design of power distribution systems to improve overall performance, reliability, and efficiency is the challenge of re-configuring distribution networks. The objectives of this process are to reduce power loss, enhance system resilience, integrate renewable energy sources, improve voltage profiles, and accommodate dynamic loads. To adapt the distribution network to shifting conditions and needs, re-configuring the network is a challenging task that calls for the use of complex optimization algorithms, smart grid technology, and real-time monitoring. It is necessary to maintain an ideal balance between several different objectives to maintain a distribution system that is both cost-effective and sustainable. The study delves into existing optimization strategies, technological advancements, and operational constraints to provide a compre-hensive review of cutting-edge distribution system reconfiguration strategies.

articleTitle: An Overview of Wireless Avionics Intra-Aircraft Communications: Latency and Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The use of wireless networks for intra-aircraft communication has garnered significant attention, with the goal of increasing efficiency and flexibility while decreasing weight, fuel consumption, and maintenance costs compared to traditional wired avionics systems. The key question is whether wireless solutions will offer reliability and latency satisfying intra-aircraft applications requirements. This survey reviews the current state of wireless solutions in terms of reliability and latency as a potential fit for intra-aircraft communications, and identifies future research directions to improve these metrics.

articleTitle: Degradation Detection on Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) Calls Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Degradation in speech on VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) refers to any deterioration in the quality of the audio during a VoIP call. This degradation can manifest in various forms, including distortion, delay, jitter, packet loss, echo, background noise, and so on. Detecting degradation in VoIP calls is crucial for the following several reasons such as improving user experience and satisfaction, boosting the effective communication and collaboration, impacting productivity and efficiency, allowing providers to proactively address issues and maintain service quality, helping network administrators to identify the root causes of quality issues and implementing solutions to improve performance and reliability. Overall, detecting degradation in speech on VoIP is essential for ensuring high-quality communication, maintaining customer satisfaction, and optimizing the performance of VoIP systems and networks. In this work, focus on detecting degradations on voice over VoIP using deep learning algorithms, namely, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs). To show the effectiveness of the models, TCD- VoIP dataset is carried out during the experiments. Experiment results demonstrate that the inclusion of deep learning methodologies exhibits remarkable experiment results.

articleTitle: Comparing Player Rating Awarding Systems: Evaluating Performance Metrics in Soccer: An in-Depth Analysis of Rating Methodologies and Their Impact on Player Assessment and Team Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The primary objective of this paper is to develop a method for accurately and consistently rating football players. A secondary objective is to evaluate the suitability of artificial neural networks for this purpose, particularly with the available data. To address these objectives, data was collected from various sources, including APIs and the WhoScored website via web scraping. Multiple solutions were explored for implementing the player rating system, encompassing both AI-based and mathe-matical approaches. In the pursuit of AI-based models, ratings provided by WhoScored were utilized as a target due to their recognized precision and consistency. Following the implemen-tation of various models, comprehensive testing and evaluation using diverse metrics and methods were conducted to identify the most effective approach, or determine if certain models are better suited for specific scenarios. Overall, this research contributes to the integration of data from multiple sources to enhance player rating methodologies in football analysis.

articleTitle: A Virtual Machine Management Platform in Computer Science Education
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The hands-on part of computer science education involves a heterogeneous environment, where students use different software, different operating systems or even different hardware for the studied subjects. The traditional approach involves deploying these environments on physical computing machines, such as lab computers or students personal computers. The current paper proposal is to move this deployment in the cloud, enabling higher usability, efficient resource allocation and more control of the learning environment by the teacher. The solution is based on a Virtual Machine Management platform and a web interface that can both be deployed in the university cloud, enabling access to virtually any computer with network access. The tests and experiments performed show that the proposed system is efficient, reliable and secure.

articleTitle: Detecting Abnormal Record in Automotive Maintenance Data Based on Deep Sparse Auto-Encoder
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: With the rapid development of automotive usage and maintenance services, the expansion of the automotive maintenance data scale inevitably brings about abnormal records,these records raise serious problems for the automotive maintenance industries. This paper proposes a new approach based on the deep sparse auto-encoder to deal with huge amounts of automotive maintenance data in reality. The failure description, maintenance project, and maintenance parts in the data are firstly vectorized using advanced text representation algorithms. Besides the measurement information in the original data, the obtained dataset has more actual semantic information to enhance the data correlation. The dataset is then pre-processed with normalization to improve the performance of the learning model.A developed deep sparse auto-encoder (DSAE) detection method is finally arranged for abnormal automotive maintenance records. The first layer of the deep sparse auto-encoder is adapted with a sparse suppression to match the dataset features. The results show that the developed deep sparse auto-encoder model can correctly identify the abnormal records, which achieves accuracy, precision, F1-Score, recall, and ROC-AUC as 99.2%, 99.9%, 97.4%, 99.6%, and 97.6%, respectively. The proposed model is further compared with other benchmark methods, the developed deep sparse auto-encoder model performs better in terms of handling the abnormal automotive maintenance data and accurate detection.

articleTitle: Heart Rate-Based Prediction of Daily Activity Levels Using Wearable Devices for Home Rehabilitation Process of Cardiac Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This study aims to contribute to the literature by developing an advanced Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model that classifies and predicts the duration of patients' daily physical activities (resting, light, moderate, intense) using heart rate data. This approach is an innovative step towards personalizing cardiac rehabilitation programs and accurately monitoring patients' daily activity levels. The application of this model aims to allow healthcare professionals to objectively track patients' activity levels. Data collection was conducted at the Istanbul University - Cerrahpaşa, Cardiology Institute exercise test laboratory during the years 2023–2024. Heart rate (bpm) of the patients was recorded through a Garmin watch worn on the wrist during exercise tests conducted using the Modified Bruce Protocol. The study included patients aged between 18 and 85 with medium-risk pre-test probability for coronary artery disease. The collected data underwent preprocessing, including synchronization of heart rate data with exercise test records and removal of inconsistent or illogical data points. LSTM model was chosen for analyzing sequential data related to heart rate over time. The model consisted of two LSTM layers and one output layer, achieving a prediction accuracy of 59.1% on the test dataset. Further efforts are underway to enhance the model's performance within the project scope. This research underscores the importance of objective activity tracking and highlights the potential to fill existing gaps in this field. The developed model, based on heart rate data collected via wearables, is expected to serve as an objective tool for monitoring cardiac rehabilitation processes and daily activity levels. By evaluating data collected through wearables, the model facilitates the calculation of individuals' durations of rest, light, moderate, and high-intensity activities throughout the day, contributing to personalized health care practices.

articleTitle: Wavelet-Based Multiresolution FOPID (MRPIλDµ) Controller for Automatic Generation Control
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a Wavelet-Based Multiresolution Fractional-Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(MRPI^{\lambda}D^{\mu})$</tex> controller for Automatic Generation Control (AGC) in power systems. The proposed controller leverages the principles of multiresolution analysis and fractional calculus to achieve improved control performance and robustness. The Area Control Error (ACE) is decomposed into multiple scales using wavelet analysis, allowing for a detailed analysis of different frequency components. At each scale, fractional-order proportional, integral, and derivative actions are applied to the error signal, enabling enhanced control over complex system dynamics. The gains of the controller are optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), Stochastic Fractal Search (SFS) to achieve optimal control performance. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PSO}-MRPI^{\lambda}D^{\mu}$</tex> was able to obtain the best overall performance and the minimum Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed controller in terms of frequency regulation, disturbance rejection, and system stability when compared to conventional controllers. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MRPI^{\lambda}D^{\mu}$</tex> controller offers a promising solution for enhancing AGC performance in power systems, leading to improved system reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Survey on UAV-Assisted Wireless Communications: Challenges, Technologies, and Application
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have attracted significant attention in recent years due to their potential for several applications, including wireless communication. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) possess the capacity to function as aerial base stations, relays, or data collection equipment, hence enabling efficient and flexible wireless communication in various scenarios. This survey article provides a thorough analysis of the current state-of-the-art in wireless communication facilitated by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). This research investigates the intricacies, progressions, and pragmatic applications of incorporating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to enhance wireless communication infrastructures. The survey covers various aspects, including UAV deployment strategies, communication architectures, resource allocation, networking protocols, and regulatory considerations. Furthermore, it presents a detailed analysis of the key enabling technologies such as UAV mobility management, energy efficiency, interference mitigation, and communication range extension. Additionally, the paper discusses the emerging applications of UAV-assisted wireless communication in areas such as disaster management, rural connectivity, surveillance, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Finally, open research challenges and future directions are identified to guide researchers and practitioners in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Recommendation Approach for Efficient Requirements Elicitation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The success of software projects depends on efficient requirements engineering, especially the crucial but difficult task of requirements elicitation. The excess amount of reusable requirements can cause information overload, hindering effective retrieval and possibly leading to overlooked or irrelevant selections. This paper presents an enhanced recommendation approach that integrates item-based collaborative filtering and content-based filtering methods to tackle this issue. Our approach uses stakeholder behavior patterns of known requirements and content similarity between requirements to help engineers manage information overload and select potential requirements that effectively meet their project objectives. Comprehensive evaluation using the RALIC and sparse datasets shows substantial enhancements in recommendation accuracy and coverage when compared to benchmark recommendation methods. Our proposed approach effectively addresses the data sparsity issue, a common challenge in recommendation systems. This study improves the efficiency and effectiveness of requirements elicitation, ultimately boosting the success of software development projects.

articleTitle: Exploring the Dynamics of Cryptocurrency Donations by Blockchain Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Donors increasingly use cryptocurrencies to support charitable causes with the underlying blockchain technology maintaining an anonymity-preserved, readily-accessible and re-liable record of transactions being made. This record can be analysed to extract information about donor behaviour for any given cause and to adapt fund-raising strategies for charities working on that cause. For example, donor fatigue that negatively impacts non-profitable organisations can be deduced in early stages and mitigation be put in place. This paper focuses on Bit-coin blockchain data and demonstrates how this and other useful information can be extracted using off-the-shelf technologies and Time Series analyses. For demonstration, it analyses the two-year long Bitcoin data available on donations made for the Ukrainian Cause. It illustrates the impact of various factors, such as the market value of Bitcoin, on donation behaviour since February 2022.

articleTitle: On the Performance of A.I-Based Cyber Incident Notification System (AICINS)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The possibility of cyber incidents is growing daily as a result of the interconnectedness of the technological gadgets used throughout the world. Artificial intelligence has emerged as a viable strategy for the notification and prevention of cyber incidents in this risk environment. This paper introduces the Artificial Intelligence Based Cyber Incident Notification System (AICINS) created to address cyber issues. AICINS uses machine learning algorithms to enable preventive responses to cyber incidents as well as real-time monitoring and analysis of such incidents. The study relied on Neova Participation Insurance Company's Domain Name System (DNS) Sense and Symantec Endpoint Protection (SEP) data. Furthermore, innovative analytical techniques have been explored in order to uncover trends that allow for the early detection of possible threats before they escalate into large-scale attacks. Relying on the performance results of commonly used ML algorithms studied, we show that the AICINPP with Random Forest Classifier may reach up a success rate of 92%.
